title: Wringer verification-set receipt
description: `set.json` — one combined result over SEVERAL sealed `wring verify` bundles of the SAME revision, written by `wring verify --set DIR…` and `wring audit --set DIR…`. Not a bundle and not a delivery: it is a receipt over bundles that already exist, it runs nothing, and it adds no measurement of its own. **The question it exists to answer.** A real project verifies in phases — a build subset, a database subset, a browser subset — because the phases need different services and different amounts of time. Each phase writes its own sealed bundle saying `passed`, and until this record existed nothing in the product could add them up: the 19 September 2026 ZenJev build combined four bundles into a ten-gate claim with a custom script and a hand-written table, and the completeness of that claim lived only in the operator's head. **What it claims.** `complete` here is STRICTER than the same word in `wringer.selection.v1`: a set is complete only when every required declared gate has EXACTLY ONE passed execution across the whole set. A single bundle's `complete` is about execution alone, because a bundle is a record of what happened; a set is a claim that a revision was verified, so a failure or a gap breaks it. The two words are different on purpose and each record says which it means. **What it refuses.** Combining is legitimate only when the bundles are speaking about the same thing, so the combiner refuses, by a sentence naming the offending bundle, when: two bundles record different `head_sha`; two bundles carry different `.wringer.yaml` bytes; a gate's check identity in `checks.json` differs between two bundles; a bundle's digest inventory does not validate; or two bundles record an outcome for the same gate. That last one is not pedantry — two outcomes for one gate is either a re-run whose order nobody recorded or two different machines disagreeing, and picking one silently is how a red becomes a green. **What it does not claim.** It does not establish that the checks cover the requirement they are bound to, that the tested source is the published source, or that a human judged anything; those are `wringer.acceptance.v3`, the delivery anchor and a recorded judgement respectively, and the generated `HANDOFF.md` beside this file says which of them are absent rather than filling them in. It reads operator-named directories and executes nothing from them.

set_id.description: This receipt's own identity, in the same timestamp-and-suffix shape as a run id. A set is re-derivable from its bundles, so this names the act of combining rather than any new measurement.

at.description: When the set was combined, ISO 8601. Not a measurement of the checks, which carry their own `started_at`; a clock reading on the machine that combined them and not authenticated.

head_sha.description: The one revision every bundle in the set agrees it tested. A set with two revisions does not exist — the combiner refuses before writing this file.

config_sha256.description: sha256 of the one `.wringer.yaml` every bundle in the set carried. The declared-gate population is read from these bytes, so the set's denominator is a hashed artefact and not a config on the combining machine, which may be a different checkout or no checkout at all.

declared.description: Every gate id in the carried `.wringer.yaml`, in declared order.

required.description: The declared gates that are not `optional: true`, in declared order. The set's denominator.

bundles.description: One row per bundle combined, in the order the operator named them.

path.description: The directory as the operator named it, verbatim. A reader who wants to re-derive the set needs the words that were typed, not a normalisation of them.

executed.description: The gates this bundle recorded a result for, in declared order.

selection_record.description: The version of the sibling record the bundle carried, or `absent` when it carried none. Bundles written before that record existed are combined from their gate results alone, which is the same population the sibling would have reported; saying which route was used keeps an older bundle readable without pretending it carried a record it never had.

executions.description: One row per gate execution across the whole set, in declared gate order: which bundle recorded it and what it recorded. The audit trail behind `passed`, `failed` and `missing_required` — a reader disputing the set's verdict for one gate can go straight to the bundle that decided it.

bundle.description: The bundle path, as named, that recorded this execution.

passed.description: Required declared gates with a passed execution somewhere in the set, in declared order.

failed.description: Required declared gates whose execution in the set failed, in declared order. A nonempty list makes the set incomplete; it is kept separate from `missing_required` because a gate that ran and failed is a finding and a gate that never ran is a gap, and the two need different next steps.

missing_required.description: Required declared gates with no execution anywhere in the set, in declared order.

complete.description: True only when `missing_required` and `failed` are both empty, so every required declared gate has exactly one passed execution across the set. Duplicate executions cannot reach this field: the combiner refuses them.

reason.description: The sentence a person reads, carried verbatim so the receipt, the generated handoff and stdout all print the same words.

limits.description: What this receipt does NOT claim, travelling with it. Pinned by CONTENT in the tests.
